section.title: Introduction
section.p: The server application can implement complex functions relying on the conservation of object identity in the framework. Such an example is the notification of business object changes to all interested client applications. Therefore the notification framework registers change listeners on the business objects and expect to be notified when a change happens. Therefore the tranfer framework should not replaced existing instances with new instances received from a client.

It should be evident that the new instances are not a problem for the persistent framework because the used concept identity is based on the class of the object and an identity property defined for each persistent object. This approach is coherant with all major persistent frameworks such as OJB, Hibernate, JDO, or J2EE enterprise beans.

This document will show different approaches to reconciliate the different concepts described above. Two main directions were identified. First a dedicated manager is provided to detect object changes and propagates them. A listener can register his interest to an object or to a property of an object. Each time a changed version of this object is received the manager is informed. The object is identified through the persistent identifier defined as the class of the object and a distinct number identifier managed in the persistent layer. Second instead of transmitting whole object the client could just propagates the changes it did. An interesting question is to determine where this logic should be executed, on client side or on server side.

section.title: Change Propagation
section.p: The change propagation is to detect the modifications in a graph of data objects and apply them to the reference data object graph. After executing the transformation both graph should be equivalent. This is only guaranteed if the order of the transformation is not relevant. Therefore as stated in the original description of the DOG framewok it is prohibited to implement business logic in property accessors. The potential changes are the following ones.

dl.dd: This is the simplest changes. The new value of the property is applied to the reference object. The change is performed using the set operation to insure that registered listeners are called. If a veto exception is thrown an application exceiption is thrown indicating that incompatible business rules are applied. It is the responsibility of the application is define smaller change jobs compatible with its logic.

A new root object was created and perhaps child objects were added to it. The framework checks that all objects are new ones. If not an exception is thrown. The propagation can only consolidate two similar graphs. This restriction is reasonable because the application can always provide a root containing all used objects. The drawback of this approach is the quantity of information to transfer. The application can tune it by deciding where the change collection logic is executed.
The object and its children were removed from the graph.
dl.dt: Add an object to an indexed property
dl.dd: Two situations arise. The inserted object is a new one. The same rules applies to it as to the situation where a new root is created. The inserted object is an existing one. Therefore the object must first be removed from the indexed property containing it and when added to the new indexed property.

section.p: The whole change propagation mechanisms build on the following assumptions.

ul.li: A data object is uniquely identified with its programming language class and a numerical identifier
A data object is a new one only if the numerical identifier has a null value

section.title: Algorithm Description
section.p: First the data object of the original graph are collected. If the root is new, all objects in the graph must be new ones. If this case all objects are persisted and the next steps are not performed.
Second for each visited object in the modified graph the rules are applied.

ul.li:
For each simple or indexed property which type is not an instance of data object we check if the property has changed. If yes the property is synchronized. The update operation is
original.set(simple-property, modified.get(simple-property))
original.set(indexed-property, modified.get(indexed-property))

For each simple property which type is an instance of data object we check if the property was set to null. If yes the property is synchronized.
original.set(simple-property, null)

For each indexed property which type is an instance of data object we check if an item was removed. If yes the indexed property is synchronized.
original.remove(data-object)

For each simple property which type is an instance of data object we check if the property was set to another object. If yes the property is synchronized. The object can only be added if it is new or was previously removed.
original.set(data-object)

For each indexed property which type is an instance of data object we check if objects were added to the property. If yes the indexed property is synchronized. The object can only be added if it is new or was previously removed.
original.add(index, data-object)

section.p: The algorithm requires three graph traversals, one of the original graph, and two times the modified graph to first remove objects and second to add some of the removed ones. So the algorithm is O(3n).
